title: Public side information available only at the receiving desk
public:
Public side information available only at the receiving desk

Five jobs require five distinct exact decisions, indexed 1 through 5. The sender sees the job. Independently, the receiver is supplied one of the public cards {1,2}, {2,3}, {3,4}, {4,5}, {5,1} containing the job. Both incident cards are possible for each job. The sender does not see which card arrived. It sends one deterministic symbol and the receiver must recover the job for every allowed combination. A proposed appendix caption gives the necessary alphabet size as the largest card size. Decide what claim and decoding rule the editor can support here.

This public mathematical stress test is an author-defined appendix example.

title: Tolerance of a public decision to a one-unit readout error
public:
Tolerance of a public decision to a one-unit readout error

A job specifies an inclusive allowable interval for the realized integer decision. The three jobs accept [0,4], [3,7] and [4,8], respectively. The sender knows the job; the receiver executes the integer command represented by the sender's symbol. Any command x can be realized as x−1, x or x+1. Nominal command 4 was compatible with every job in an error-free run. Decide what uniform guarantee survives this error model. If more than one command is needed, what is the fewest distinct commands and a workable assignment?

public:
Replacing a source note with ordinary adaptive remeasurement

title: Robustness of three decision messages to a substitution
public:
Robustness of three decision messages to a substitution

The receiving appendix desk needs one of three mutually exclusive decisions. All messages have the same length n in binary digits, and at most one transmitted digit may flip; zero flips must also work. There is no other side information or repeat request. We need the shortest fixed length for guaranteed recovery, with an implementation or checkable construction. Is a four-digit line sufficient? Decide the shortest line the editor can promise.

title: Sensitivity of the observed ordering to additional major reports among completers
public:
Sensitivity of the observed ordering to additional major reports among completers

Keep reproduction, human-only outcomes and all recorded positives fixed. Imagine that expanded ascertainment upgrades selected AI-arm teams from zero to ≥1 major error. For the joint outcome 'reproduced and reported ≥1 accepted major error', could the assisted rate reach or exceed the observed human-only rate and, separately, could the led rate? Give the fewest upgrades where possible and a sharp upper bound where impossible. This sensitivity scenario makes no claim that any additional report was actually missed.

The public extract below contains one retained team per line, with no team identifiers. Its columns are assigned collaboration mode (0 human only, 1 AI-assisted, 2 AI-led), successful reproduction (0 or 1), and number of accepted major errors reported by that team. A zero is the released coding for no accepted report. The article also reported an adjusted comparison of the number of major errors. The three-column extract omits event, paper and assignment-block identifiers. Source: Brodeur et al., PNAS 2026, doi:10.1073/pnas.2524747123; deidentified three-column extract adapted from I4Replication/AI-Games, revision c2721bb6c2ddfad2633d9ab0a01dc514ec956923, CC BY 4.0. The editor may use and share these figures with attribution.
